reviews.reason: The full matching-face formula requires a research-level synthesis of a geometric fiber-minimum diagonal and a combinatorial characterization of all its maximal cells. The source must establish weighted face/product structure and positivity, use a Boolean leaf-orientation quotient to rule out nonmatching cells by dimension induction over product facets, and prove the reverse inclusion by classifying adjacent maximal G-faces and propagating within a fixed Boolean fiber. The formula is not a direct consequence of ordinary face-lattice definitions, nor is the reverse inclusion automatic from the exclusion argument. H3 remains justified with the classical face-interval fact named below as background; the specialized two-direction argument remains retained proof work.
reviews.core_assessment:
Read complete selected ranges515-755,759-808,833-1044,1343-1380,1390-1660 before consulting the selector difficulty reason. Also read1045-1117,1381-1389,1661-1666 to check whether the omitted boundary explanation appeared adjacently; it did not. Native TikZ source for the tree rotations and neighboring faces was read as part of these ranges. No rendered-page QA is claimed.
The weighted construction assigns each leaf-pair product to its least common ancestor, giving the hyperplane identity and interval inequalities. Tight compatible intervals produce planar-tree faces and the displayed coordinate permutation identifies each facet with two lower weighted Loday factors. The positive orientation argument rewrites an edge direction in the consecutive-difference basis; facet equalities identify or kill basis coefficients, so a one-dimensional solution has a common nonzero coefficient on a subset. Every decreasing orientation vector gives the same sign. The minor printed sign/index slips are recorded below.
The averaging projection beta has fibers x+y=2z, identified with P intersect(2z-P). Positive orientation makes the chosen linear functional attain its minimum at a unique vertex in each such intersection. The lower-face coherent subdivision is therefore tight, and its section is the stated diagonal. Restriction to an exposed face follows from the fact that a midpoint in that face forces both endpoints into the face. Purity and full dimension of its maximal cells are elementary facts about the resulting finite subdivision of a polytope.
The movement lemma is valid with the line quotient parallel to e_i, which the author subsequent argument uniquely specifies. With the printed identity projection it is false as a lower/upper-face assertion. Under the line quotient, lower and upper sections are connected, an edge crossing from L_i=0 to1 collapses under projection and so cannot lie in either section, and a vertex must be an endpoint of its line fiber. Thus the lower vertices are exactly L_i=0 and upper vertices exactly L_i=1. A relative face interior meeting neither lower section allows the required small displacement. This is the same subsequent author argument with its necessary projection identified, not an alternative movement proof.
For exclusion, L(top F) not<=L(bottom G) gives simultaneous opposite e_i motions preserving the midpoint and decreasing the fiber objective. In the remaining case, corrected dimension counts force F=F_s, G=G_t and L(s)=L(t). A common facet contains s,t. Intersecting with it and using purity either violates the dimension bound or embeds the intersections in a maximal cell of the lower-dimensional product. The coordinate permutation preserves the relevant orientation, and a putative order relation in all graft factors would imply r<=u, contrary to the chosen extrema. This closes the first inclusion by induction.
For the reverse inclusion, the unique matching maximal cell containing(t,t) is F_t times G_t, because any other matching extrema would satisfy t<=r<=v<=t. For t prec u with equal Boolean value, the source tree construction gives B=G_t intersect G_u as a facet of both, with u in B and t not in B; B is not itself a maximal G_v, and only G_t/G_u contain it as a facet. The boundary sentence1651 is an abbreviated application of the classical face-interval property, detailed in its issue record below. Once beta(H) is interior, an adjacent maximal cell exists on the other side. Product-facet alternatives and the neighboring-face classification force that cell to be F_s times G_u. A saturated Tamari chain between equal Boolean endpoints stays in that same Boolean fiber by monotonicity, completing the propagation.
reviews.prerequisite_assessment: The permitted convex-polytope, subdivision and tree/Tamari background does not provide the magical formula, tightness, Boolean exclusion or neighboring-cell classification. The classical additional precision needed at1651 is that the binary refinements of a planar tree form the Tamari interval between its left-comb and right-comb refinements. This fact is stated explicitly in Chatel-Pilaud-Pons, The weak order on integer posets, ALCO2(1)(2019), p22, section2.2.3, DOI10.5802/alco.36; I opened that primary PDF and read the exact passage. It should be named in the task background rather than left implicit. It supplies only order convexity of a face, not the special diagonal conclusion. The author native formulas and all local proof obligations remain unchanged.

editorial_notes: The movement lemma1450 prints id:P->P. That literal identity would make every fiber a singleton and every face both lower and upper, so it is not the map used by the ensuing argument. Lines1463–1464 require an edge parallel to e_i to be vertical, and1474–1475 require line-segment fibers. These uniquely specify the affine-span quotient along span(e_i), up to affine coordinates in the quotient, with height psi=<x,e_i>. Retain the printed id and disclose this reading; no new movement proof is inserted.

With the definitions1509, r_t counts right-leaning leaves minus k and l_t counts left-leaning leaves minus k. The original contraction recipe1513 gives dim F_t=r_t and dim G_t=l_t. The displays1509 and1522–1524 exchange these two letters. The recipe, author formulas and proof are retained; the letter convention just stated is the one compatible with the construction and with the inequality r_s+l_t<=d used there.

The edge-direction calculation877 has the dot-product difference reversed: the displayed earlier +x/later -x edge pairs as x(v_i-v_(i+j))>0. The consecutive-difference sum at888 also has its initial index offset: the source basis886 gives a_(p+q-1)-a_p for coordinates p+1,...,p+q-1, with endpoint coefficients0. These are source-determined sign/index readings; the equal-or-zero coefficient argument is unchanged. At1437 the edge is indeed a positive multiple of e_i, but the scalar is the product of the total weights of the two outside subtrees, not in general the product of two individual leaf weights. The subsequent movement proof uses only positive parallelism. Preserve all printed formulas; do not certify the printed scalar as an exact general value.

At1005 the right-hand map on the lower faces of tilde P is pr, as fixed by the domains and factorization978–982 and the immediately following sentence; tilde-pi has domain Q. This is a cellwise affine homeomorphism on the lower graph, not a claim that the entire piecewise-linear graph is one affine subspace. The original display is retained.

The boundary sentence1651 is compressed. Its order-theoretic input is the classical Tamari face-interval property explicitly listed in standard_prerequisites. It applies to the s<=t<u vertices and B=G_t intersect G_u from the author preceding construction; the conclusion also uses the already proved tightness and full dimension of the current maximal cell. This is an explanation of the scope of the omitted classical convex/order step, not a replacement author proof. The specialized neighbor classification and propagation remain solution obligations.

The counted formula has n>=2 as in582–584; the arity-one operadic unit635 is a separate convention, not an n-2=-1 instance. In product-facet induction omit point factors when choosing a facet and apply the Boolean-fiber facet argument only in positive dimension. The author treats dimensions0 and1 separately at1529; no facet-containing-vertex assertion for a point is made.
